stories.headline: CrowdStrike Shares Fall 10% After a $44 Billion Zscaler Deal Despite an Earnings Beat and Raised Guidance
stories.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., explains why shares of CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) fell about 10% on Monday, November 23, while most tech stocks rallied. The trigger was a proposed acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) for about $44 billion, announced the same morning. The sell-off came despite a strong report. CrowdStrike posted revenue growth of 28.3% against expectations of 23.9%, and EPS of $0.34 against $0.31. It also raised full-year guidance. Bleeker points to the deal instead: Zscaler's wide product line may be hard to integrate into CrowdStrike's platform, and the roughly 34% premium arrives when cybersecurity stocks are richly valued. Zscaler shares rose about 16%, while CrowdStrike is now down 26% from its recent highs. Bleeker lays out both cases. The bull case is that cybersecurity budgets must rise as companies patch systems, with outages at Apple and others as examples. The bear case is that frontier AI models may become the center of cyber defense, which raises questions about what companies like CrowdStrike offer. Expect choppy trading in these shares while investors sort that out.

stories.headline: Stocks Roar as the S&P 500 Jumps About 4.5% on News Jensen Huang Is Returning as NVIDIA CEO
stories.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., covers a broad Monday rally led by chip stocks. The S&P 500 was up about 4.5% in midday trading, after news broke that Jensen Huang will return as CEO of NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA). The IT sector gained 8.6%, while financials rose 1.7%, utilities 0.96% and health care 0.9%. Real estate and energy declined. The State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA: SPY) rose about 4.5%. Chips drove the move. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ: SOXX) gained 12.9%, led by NVIDIA, which was up more than 30%. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (Cboe: IGV) rose about 4%, so software stocks reacted far less than chip stocks. The GraniteShares 2x Long NVIDIA Daily ETF (NASDAQ: NVDL) jumped 60% but is still down nearly 50% over the past month. NVIDIA traded around $180 before Huang's ouster and hasn't recovered that level. Many stocks bouncing 20% or more today fell 20% or more at the end of last week. Watch whether this is a relief rally or the start of a recovery after the market rotated out of AI and into defensive sectors.
